children: Malaysian palm oil futures eased on Friday, erasing earlier gains and adding to a weekly loss, on rising stockpiles, although concerns over future supply tightness helped cushion the decline.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange was down 11 ringgit, or 0.23%, at 4,874 ringgit ($1,197.54) a metric ton by the midday break.
The contract has fallen 1.12% so far this week after last week's 0.72% gain.
Malaysia's palm oil inventories hit an eight-month high in August as production climbed to the highest level since December and exports declined, data from the industry regulator showed on Thursday.
The larger-than-expected inventory build reflects a widening imbalance between recovering seasonal production and softer export demand, a CIMB Securities research report said.
"The higher stock level could cap near-term crude palm oil price upside, although downside may remain cushioned if biological tree stress continues to constrain production growth," it said.
It pointed out that production will likely remain seasonally firm in the coming months, though a meaningful recovery in exports will be important to prevent inventories from rising further.
Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products for September 1 to 10 fell between 11.7% and 17.5% from a month earlier.

Oil prices rose and both major benchmarks are on track to end the week above $100 a barrel for the first time since mid-May, as increasing attacks along key shipping routes in the Middle East fuel fears of a prolonged disruption to supplies. O/R
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.44%, while its palm oil contract
shed 0.79%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were down 0.43%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
